texto: Her last message said: We are holding our own. Minutes later, she was gone.
The Edmund Fitzgerald was seven hundred and twenty-nine feet long, the biggest ship on the Great Lakes when she was launched.
On November tenth, 1975, she was crossing Lake Superior with twenty-nine men, in a storm that kept getting worse.
At three thirty, she reported a list, and damage on deck. Then she lost both radars.
So another ship, the Arthur M. Anderson, became her eyes, ten miles behind her, reading her position out over the radio.
At ten past seven, they asked how she was doing. She said she was holding her own.
Then the snow lifted. The men on the Anderson could see lights twenty miles away. The Fitzgerald should have been right there, ten miles ahead.
There was nothing. Nothing on the radar. No mayday. No wreckage in sight.
The Coast Guard blamed the hatches. The full video shows why many still disagree.
